lesson_title: Four Things, One Bowl, Zero Tweezers
hook_text: Beans, iron filings, sand and salt, all stirred into one bowl. Can you get every one back out?
clip_script: Here is the trick: in a mixture, nothing is joined. Every part is still itself, so you use its differences. Step one: the beans are big, so a sieve or your fingers pull them out. Step two: iron is magnetic. Wave a magnet wrapped in plastic and the filings jump onto it. Step three: add water and stir. Salt dissolves. Sand does not. Step four: pour it through filter paper. The sand stays on the paper; that is the residue. Salty water drips through; that is the filtrate. Step five: dry out the water and salt crystals appear. Gold panners used the same idea at Pilgrim's Rest: swirl gravel in water and the heavy gold stays behind. Different property, different method.
visual_style: Whiteboard bowl with four coloured ingredients; a sieve, a magnet, a funnel with filter paper and an evaporating dish appearing in sequence; a gold pan with shining grains.
pacing: Quick five-step sequence with a tidy gold-pan bonus.
